name: Boltz-1 and Boltz-2 (Boltz PBC)
subcategory: open AF3-class biomolecular structure and binding-affinity models
origin_detail: Released from the GitHub repo jwohlwend/boltz (Jeremy Wohlwend and co-authors); commercialised by 'Boltz PBC' (boltz.com). The academic (MIT) origin is widely reported but was not confirmed on fetched pages.

licences.weights: MIT (Boltz-1, Boltz-2); BoltzProt-1 and BoltzMol-1 proprietary
licences.data: Boltz-1 processed PDB and OpenFold distillation data downloadable (licence not stated)

openness_notes: README: 'Our model and code are released under MIT License, and can be freely used for both academic and commercial purposes.' The Boltz-1 training guide provides pre-processed RCSB PDB structures, PDB MSAs (ColabFold) and 'the OpenFold self-distillation set' for download (about 250 GB, licence not stated); Boltz-2 training code is 'coming soon'. As of 2026-11-23, boltz.com labels Boltz-2 and BoltzGen open-source but BoltzProt-1 and BoltzMol-1 proprietary, running on Boltz Lab (cloud, dedicated or on-premises). Initial 4 (MIT code and weights with reproducible training data); current 2 (open core: open older models, proprietary newest models and platform).

license_history.note: bioRxiv 2025.06.14 identifier; HF boltz-community/boltz-2 tagged MIT.

license_history.license: Proprietary BoltzProt-1 and BoltzMol-1 on Boltz Lab
license_history.note: Shown on boltz.com 2026-11-23; launch date not confirmed.

relicensing_events.to: Boltz-1 MIT (code, weights, training data pipeline)
relicensing_events.outcome_note: An open AF3-class model released about six months after AF3's restricted launch.

relicensing_events.to: Open core: newest models (BoltzProt-1, BoltzMol-1) proprietary
relicensing_events.outcome_note: Coincides with company formation and a $110M Series A (announced 2026-11-18). Existing MIT releases remain open.

funding_as_of: 2026-11-18: $110M Series A announced (investors not named; earlier rounds not confirmed)
risk_events: Shift to proprietary models after a VC round; Boltz-2 training code still 'coming soon'
robustness: MIT-licensed Boltz-1/2 weights and Boltz-1 training data can be forked regardless of the company's future choices.
physical_science_relevance: Protein-ligand structure and affinity prediction for medicinal chemistry; used by 'top 20 pharma' per the company.

training_data.name: RCSB PDB (mmCIF)
training_data.note: Pre-processed structures provided for Boltz-1 training.

openness_effect_assessment: An MIT licence for an AF3-class model gave Boltz fast adoption (5M+ downloads and 1,000+ companies by its own count) and positioned it as the default open alternative to AF3. That user base preceded a $110M Series A and a turn to proprietary successor models, the open-core pattern familiar from software.
key_takeaway: Boltz shows the lifecycle of an open clone: an academic MIT release fills the gap left by a restricted corporate model, wins users, becomes a company and then closes its newest models. Labs should pin MIT versions and keep the training data, which remain usable whatever the company does.
